breeds.name: Ameraucana
breeds.broodiness: Rarely goes broody (seldom sits on eggs to hatch them)
breeds.genetics_notes: Blue shell from the oocyan (O) allele: an EAV-HP retroviral insertion upstream of SLCO1B3 makes the shell gland deposit biliverdin through the whole shell, so the inside is blue too. Dominant.
breeds.breeding_notes: One copy of the blue allele is enough; crossed onto a brown layer, daughters that inherit it lay green/olive.

general_citations.excerpt: Blue eggshell (oocyan) is caused by an EAV-HP insertion that up-regulates SLCO1B3 in the shell gland, increasing biliverdin uptake.

general_citations.excerpt: Independent confirmation of the EAV-HP insertion in South American blue-egg fowl.

general_citations.excerpt: Brown color is protoporphyrin IX, concentrated in the outer shell and cuticle; color intensity tends to decline with hen age.

glossary.definition: The dominant blue-eggshell allele. One copy makes the whole shell blue, inside and out.
A transporter gene. The blue-shell insertion switches it on in the shell gland so that biliverdin is taken up into the shell.
An endogenous avian retrovirus. Its insertion near SLCO1B3 is the cause of blue eggs, found in both Chinese and Mapuche fowl.
The blue-green pigment in blue eggshells.
The brown pigment, laid mainly in the outer shell and cuticle. It usually lightens as a hen ages.
The thin organic coat on a freshly laid egg. On brown eggs it carries much of the pigment.
A blue shell with brown pigment over it. Usually from a dark-brown × blue cross.
A cross of a regular brown layer and a blue layer, not a recognized breed. Egg color varies from hen to hen.
A breed whose chicks can be sexed at hatch by down color or pattern, e.g. Cream Legbar.
A broody hen wants to sit on eggs and hatch them. Breeds differ: some rarely go broody, others often do. Hatcheries rate how likely each breed is.
A traditional breed tracked on The Livestock Conservancy priority list (Critical, Watch, Recovering, etc.).

pairings.explanation: Purebred Ameraucanas carry two copies of the dominant blue allele, so every first-generation daughter gets one and lays a blue shell under heavy brown pigment: olive. Brown-only layers can appear in later generations.
Koops Coops crossed Cream Legbar with French Cuckoo Marans for olive eggers. The shade varies between sage and olive.
pairings.variety_note: The source used French Cuckoo Marans, not Black Copper Marans.

pairings.explanation: Koops Coops crossed these to aim for speckled green eggs. Speckling is not guaranteed.
Crossing a brown layer with a blue layer produces Easter Eggers. Egg color varies from hen to hen.
Leghorns add no brown pigment, so daughters carrying the dominant blue allele should lay blue (inferred from genetics, not reported by a breeder).
